title: I am your student
hookLine: Krishna's answer to a man in tears is not comfort; it's a jolt, and then Arjuna asks to be taught
carry: the teaching begins when you ask: teach me
tomorrow: The self that is not slain (2.11–2.25)
last: DESPAIR, TOO, IS COUNTED AS A YOGA.

lines: A FRIEND ON THE FLOOR, IN TEARS.
IT'S OKAY, YOU DON'T HAVE TO.
cards: Here's what kindness usually sounds like. A friend is on the floor in tears, saying I can't do this. Someone kneels, puts a hand on their back, and says: it's okay, you don't have to.
Now here's Krishna, with his friend in exactly that state, in the middle of a battlefield. His first words are closer to: what is this? Where did this come from?
Get up. Chapter two begins with a jolt.

teach.b: Sanjaya sets the scene: Arjuna, overcome with pity, eyes full of tears. He's already had one line from Krishna, look at them. Now come Krishna's first words of real answer.
In Sanskrit: kutas tva kashmalam idam vishame samupasthitam. Older English translators rendered it something like, whence this dejection, at this hour of crisis? Then: klaibyam ma sma gamah Partha.
Don't give in to this unmanly weakness. And: tyaktvottishtha parantapa.

teach.h: CAST IT OFF AND STAND UP.
teach.b: Cast off this petty faintness of heart and stand up, you who scorch your foes. It sounds harsh. But Krishna isn't agreeing with the story Arjuna tells about himself.
He's reminding him who he is. And it doesn't work, not yet. Arjuna argues again.
How can I shoot arrows at Bhishma and Drona, who deserve my worship? Better to live as a beggar. I don't even know which is better, winning or losing.
Then the sentence that turns the whole book: shishyas te 'ham shadhi mam tvam prapannam.

teach.h: I AM YOUR STUDENT. TEACH ME.
teach.b: I am your student. Teach me. I've come to you for refuge.
After that, he says, I will not fight, and he falls silent.
And Krishna, between the two armies, answers him, the text says, as if smiling.

teach.h: THE TEACHING BEGINS WHEN YOU ASK.
teach.b: The jolt wasn't the teaching. The jolt got Arjuna to ask. That's the shape of learning in Hinduism: the student comes to the teacher, the guru, and asks, and the Gita's whole teaching is given because Arjuna asked.

how: Commentators often treat Gita 2.7, where Arjuna says he is Krishna's student and asks to be taught, as the moment the teaching truly begins, and 2.3's call to cast off faintness and stand up is often quoted in times of discouragement.

o: arise, get back on your feet
sit down and rest a while

games.q: what's inside Krishna's first words — tap the pairs.

s: Krishna's first answer to Arjuna is gentle comfort
it's a jolt: where has this come from? cast it off and stand up.
Arjuna asks Krishna to teach him
I am your student; teach me. I've come to you for refuge.
Arjuna stands up right after Krishna's first words
he argues again, says I will not fight, and falls silent. then Krishna answers, as if smiling.

games.q: you're Arjuna. Krishna has told you to cast off your weakness and stand up. you still can't. what do you say?
o: I am your student. teach me.
games.why: he argues once more, then says: I am your student, teach me. that sentence starts the whole teaching of the Gita.

practice: Go back to the bow you set down yesterday, the thing that's too much, and instead of I can't, try a different sentence: teach me how to face this. Say it inside, to God if you pray, or to life, or to your own wiser self.
Then breathe, notice what changes in your body when you move from giving up to asking, and imagine someone answering, as if smiling.

wordCard.voice: Uttishtha. Stand up, arise — Krishna's call in Gita two, three. Where has this faintness come from, at this hour? Cast it off, and stand up.

orig.note: Sanskrit: stand up, arise. Krishna's call in Gita 2.3.

carryVoice: Your line: the teaching begins when you ask: teach me. Tomorrow, Krishna starts teaching the one who asked. See you then.
